source.title: Resolución 160/38243/2026, de 5 de mayo, de la Dirección General de la Guardia Civil, por la que se convocan pruebas selectivas para ingreso en los centros docentes de formación para la incorporación a la Escala de Cabos y Guardias del Cuerpo de la Guardia Civil (base 6.1.1)
source.publisher: Agencia Estatal Boletín Oficial del Estado

meta.notes: Preguntas originales al estilo de la prueba de conocimientos generales (4 opciones, una correcta; los errores penalizan), redactadas a partir del texto consolidado del BOE; no provienen de bancos de academias ni de exámenes. "excerpt" es el fragmento literal de la norma y "ref" el artículo.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «My brother ___ in a police station in Madrid.»
questions.explanation: En presente simple, la tercera persona del singular (he, she, it, my brother) añade -s al verbo: works. «Is work» mezcla el verbo to be con el infinitivo y es incorrecto.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «Yesterday we ___ to the beach by train.»
questions.explanation: «Yesterday» exige pasado simple. Go es irregular: go – went – gone. «Gone» es el participio y necesita un auxiliar (have gone); «goed» no existe.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «She ___ the email last night because her computer was broken.»
questions.explanation: La negativa del pasado simple se forma con did not (didn't) + infinitivo sin to: didn't send. Tras didn't el verbo nunca va en pasado.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «___ two patrol cars outside the building.»
questions.explanation: Para indicar existencia se usa there is (singular) y there are (plural). «Two patrol cars» es plural, por lo que corresponde there are.

questions.stem: Choose the correct preposition: «The exam starts ___ 9 o'clock ___ Monday.»
questions.explanation: Se usa at con horas (at 9 o'clock), on con días de la semana y fechas (on Monday) e in con meses, años y partes del día (in May, in the morning).

questions.ref: Inglés · Imperativo y vocabulario de indicaciones
questions.stem: Read the sign: «NO PARKING. Vehicles will be removed.» What does it mean?
options: You can leave your car here for free.
You can only park here at night.
You must not leave your car here.
questions.explanation: «No parking» significa prohibido aparcar, y «vehicles will be removed» advierte que los vehículos serán retirados (por la grúa). Por tanto, no se puede dejar el coche allí.

questions.ref: Inglés · Present perfect vs past simple
questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «I ___ in this city since 2019.»
questions.explanation: Con since (desde un momento concreto) o for (durante un periodo) para una situación que empezó en el pasado y continúa, se usa el present perfect: have/has + participio (have lived).

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «If you study hard, you ___ the exam.»
questions.explanation: El primer condicional expresa una condición real o probable: if + presente simple, will + infinitivo. Would se usa en el segundo condicional (if + pasado simple).

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «English ___ in many countries around the world.»
questions.explanation: La voz pasiva se forma con to be + participio. El inglés no habla, sino que es hablado: is spoken (presente simple pasivo).

questions.ref: Inglés · Must / mustn't / don't have to
questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «You ___ use your mobile phone while driving. It's illegal.»
questions.explanation: Mustn't expresa prohibición. Don't have to y needn't indican que algo no es necesario, pero no que esté prohibido.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «How ___ water do you drink every day?»
questions.explanation: Much se usa con sustantivos incontables (water, money, information) y many con contables en plural (bottles). «How a lot» no existe.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «The woman ___ called the police was very nervous.»
questions.explanation: Who (o that) introduce oraciones de relativo referidas a personas; which se refiere a cosas, whose expresa posesión y where lugar.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «I enjoy ___ in the mountains at weekends.»
questions.explanation: Algunos verbos como enjoy, finish, mind o avoid van seguidos de gerundio (-ing), no de infinitivo.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Tom starts work at 7 a.m. He usually drives to work, but today his car is at the garage, so he is taking the bus.» Which statement is true?
options: Tom always takes the bus to work.
Tom's car is broken, so he is walking to work.
Tom normally goes to work by car.
questions.explanation: «Usually drives» indica la costumbre (va en coche normalmente); «today… he is taking the bus» es una excepción de hoy. Empieza a las 7 a. m. (de la mañana), no p. m.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «When I was a child, I ___ play football every afternoon.»
questions.explanation: Used to + infinitivo expresa hábitos pasados que ya no se dan. «Be used to + -ing» significa estar acostumbrado a algo y no encaja aquí; «use to» solo aparece tras did (didn't use to).

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «When we arrived at the station, the train ___.»
questions.explanation: El past perfect (had + participio) indica una acción anterior a otra acción pasada: el tren se fue antes de que llegáramos.

questions.stem: Choose the correct reported sentence: He said, «I am tired.»
options: He said that he was tired.
He said that I am tired.
He said me that he was tired.
He told that he is tired.
questions.explanation: En estilo indirecto con said el tiempo retrocede (am → was) y el pronombre se adapta (I → he). Say no lleva objeto de persona sin to («said me» es incorrecto) y tell sí lo exige (he told me that…).

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «If they had left earlier, they ___ the accident.»
questions.explanation: El tercer condicional se refiere a situaciones pasadas que no ocurrieron: if + past perfect, would have + participio.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Visitors must show an identity document at the entrance. Children under 14 must be accompanied by an adult. Photography is allowed, except in the archive room.» Which statement is true?
options: Visitors do not need any document to enter.
Adults must be accompanied by a child.
questions.explanation: Los menores de 14 años deben ir acompañados de un adulto, así que un niño de 12 no puede entrar solo. Hay que mostrar un documento de identidad y las fotos solo están prohibidas en la sala de archivo.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Hi Laura! I'm in Salamanca now. I'm staying with my aunt and uncle in a flat near the Plaza Mayor. Yesterday I visited the cathedral and in the evening we had dinner in a small restaurant. The weather is sunny, but it's quite cold at night, so I'm happy I brought my jacket. On Saturday my cousin and I are taking the bus to Ávila. I'm going back home next Wednesday. Love, Marta.» Where is Marta staying?
options: In a hotel near the cathedral.
questions.explanation: El texto dice «I'm staying with my aunt and uncle»: se aloja con sus tíos, en un piso cerca de la Plaza Mayor.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Hi Laura! I'm in Salamanca now. I'm staying with my aunt and uncle in a flat near the Plaza Mayor. Yesterday I visited the cathedral and in the evening we had dinner in a small restaurant. The weather is sunny, but it's quite cold at night, so I'm happy I brought my jacket. On Saturday my cousin and I are taking the bus to Ávila. I'm going back home next Wednesday. Love, Marta.» What did Marta do yesterday?
options: She visited the cathedral and had dinner in a restaurant.
She took the bus to Ávila.
questions.explanation: «Yesterday I visited the cathedral and in the evening we had dinner in a small restaurant»: ayer visitó la catedral y cenó en un restaurante.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Hi Laura! I'm in Salamanca now. I'm staying with my aunt and uncle in a flat near the Plaza Mayor. Yesterday I visited the cathedral and in the evening we had dinner in a small restaurant. The weather is sunny, but it's quite cold at night, so I'm happy I brought my jacket. On Saturday my cousin and I are taking the bus to Ávila. I'm going back home next Wednesday. Love, Marta.» How will Marta travel to Ávila?
options: She is not going to Ávila.
questions.explanation: «On Saturday my cousin and I are taking the bus to Ávila»: el present continuous expresa un plan futuro ya decidido; irá en autobús con su primo o prima.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Hi Laura! I'm in Salamanca now. I'm staying with my aunt and uncle in a flat near the Plaza Mayor. Yesterday I visited the cathedral and in the evening we had dinner in a small restaurant. The weather is sunny, but it's quite cold at night, so I'm happy I brought my jacket. On Saturday my cousin and I are taking the bus to Ávila. I'm going back home next Wednesday. Love, Marta.» Which statement is true?
options: Marta is going home on Saturday.
It is cold at night in Salamanca.
questions.explanation: «It's quite cold at night, so I'm happy I brought my jacket»: hace frío por la noche y Marta sí trajo la chaqueta. Vuelve a casa el miércoles, no el sábado.

questions.stem: Read the notice: «CENTRAL STATION – LOST PROPERTY. If you have lost something on a train, please come to the Lost Property Office on Platform 1. Items are kept for 30 days. To collect an item, you must show an identity document and describe the item. Opening hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00–18:00. Closed at weekends and on public holidays. Items not collected after 30 days are given to charity.» Where should you go if you lost something on a train?
options: To the Lost Property Office on Platform 1.
questions.explanation: «Please come to the Lost Property Office on Platform 1»: hay que ir a la oficina de objetos perdidos del andén 1.

questions.stem: Read the notice: «CENTRAL STATION – LOST PROPERTY. If you have lost something on a train, please come to the Lost Property Office on Platform 1. Items are kept for 30 days. To collect an item, you must show an identity document and describe the item. Opening hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00–18:00. Closed at weekends and on public holidays. Items not collected after 30 days are given to charity.» What do you need to collect an item?
options: An identity document and a description of the item.
Nothing: you just ask for it.
questions.explanation: «You must show an identity document and describe the item»: se exige documento de identidad y describir el objeto. Must expresa obligación.

questions.stem: Read the notice: «CENTRAL STATION – LOST PROPERTY. If you have lost something on a train, please come to the Lost Property Office on Platform 1. Items are kept for 30 days. To collect an item, you must show an identity document and describe the item. Opening hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00–18:00. Closed at weekends and on public holidays. Items not collected after 30 days are given to charity.» Can you collect your item on a Sunday?
options: No, because the office is closed at weekends.
Yes, but only in the morning.
Only if it is a public holiday.
questions.explanation: El horario es de lunes a viernes y la oficina está «closed at weekends»: el domingo forma parte del fin de semana, así que está cerrada.

questions.stem: Read the notice: «CENTRAL STATION – LOST PROPERTY. If you have lost something on a train, please come to the Lost Property Office on Platform 1. Items are kept for 30 days. To collect an item, you must show an identity document and describe the item. Opening hours: Monday to Friday, 8:00–18:00. Closed at weekends and on public holidays. Items not collected after 30 days are given to charity.» What happens to an item that nobody collects in 30 days?
options: It is sent to the police.
It is kept for another 30 days.
questions.explanation: «Items not collected after 30 days are given to charity»: la pasiva are given indica que se entregan a una organización benéfica.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Last winter Daniel was driving through the mountains when it started to snow heavily. He couldn't see the road, so he stopped in a small village. A family who lived there offered him a room for the night. The next morning the snowplough had cleared the road and he continued his journey. Since then, Daniel has visited the family every summer.» Why did Daniel stop in the village?
options: Because he couldn't see the road in the heavy snow.
Because he wanted to visit a family.
Because the village was his destination.
questions.explanation: «It started to snow heavily. He couldn't see the road, so he stopped»: so introduce la consecuencia; paró porque la nevada no le dejaba ver la carretera.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Last winter Daniel was driving through the mountains when it started to snow heavily. He couldn't see the road, so he stopped in a small village. A family who lived there offered him a room for the night. The next morning the snowplough had cleared the road and he continued his journey. Since then, Daniel has visited the family every summer.» Where did Daniel sleep that night?
options: In a hotel in the mountains.
In a room offered by a family in the village.
questions.explanation: «A family who lived there offered him a room for the night»: durmió en una habitación que le ofreció una familia del pueblo.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Last winter Daniel was driving through the mountains when it started to snow heavily. He couldn't see the road, so he stopped in a small village. A family who lived there offered him a room for the night. The next morning the snowplough had cleared the road and he continued his journey. Since then, Daniel has visited the family every summer.» What does «the snowplough had cleared the road» mean?
options: A machine had removed the snow from the road before he left.
The road was still closed because of the snow.
It snowed again in the morning.
questions.explanation: Snowplough es la máquina quitanieves y clear significa despejar. El past perfect (had cleared) indica que la carretera ya estaba despejada cuando Daniel siguió su viaje.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Last winter Daniel was driving through the mountains when it started to snow heavily. He couldn't see the road, so he stopped in a small village. A family who lived there offered him a room for the night. The next morning the snowplough had cleared the road and he continued his journey. Since then, Daniel has visited the family every summer.» Which statement is true now?
options: Daniel visited the family only once.
Daniel lives in the village now.
Daniel visits the family every winter.
Daniel still visits the family every summer.
questions.explanation: «Since then, Daniel has visited the family every summer»: el present perfect con since expresa algo que empezó en el pasado y sigue hasta hoy; sigue visitándolos cada verano.

questions.stem: Read the message: «Hi Sam, just to let you know that the team meeting has been moved from Thursday to Friday because the manager is ill. It will start at 10:30 instead of 9:00. Please bring last week's report. Thanks, Alex.» When is the meeting now?
questions.explanation: «Moved from Thursday to Friday» y «at 10:30 instead of 9:00»: la reunión es ahora el viernes a las 10:30. Instead of significa «en lugar de».

questions.stem: Read the message: «Hi Sam, just to let you know that the team meeting has been moved from Thursday to Friday because the manager is ill. It will start at 10:30 instead of 9:00. Please bring last week's report. Thanks, Alex.» Why was the meeting changed?
options: Because the report is not ready.
Because Alex is busy on Thursday.
questions.explanation: «Because the manager is ill»: se cambió porque el responsable está enfermo (ill = enfermo).

questions.stem: Choose the correctly spelled word.
questions.explanation: Beautiful se escribe con «eau» (de beauty) y el sufijo -ful lleva una sola l.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled incorrectly?
questions.explanation: Regla «i before e, except after c»: tras c se escribe ei (received, receipt); en los demás casos, ie (believe, piece). Lo correcto es received.

questions.stem: Choose the correct plural of «baby».
questions.explanation: Los sustantivos acabados en consonante + y forman el plural cambiando y por i y añadiendo -es: baby → babies (pero boy → boys, porque la y va tras vocal).

questions.stem: Choose the correct -ing form of «run».
questions.explanation: En los verbos de una sílaba acabados en una vocal + una consonante se duplica la consonante final antes de -ing: run → running, swim → swimming.

questions.stem: Choose the correctly spelled day of the week.
questions.explanation: Wednesday lleva una d que no se pronuncia (Wed-nes-day). En inglés los días de la semana se escriben siempre con mayúscula inicial.

questions.stem: Choose the correctly spelled word.
questions.explanation: Necessary lleva una sola c y dos s (ne-ce-ssa-ry).

questions.stem: Choose the correctly spelled word.
questions.explanation: Accommodation lleva doble c y doble m (ac-com-mo-da-tion).

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «A motorway is usually ___ than a country road.»
questions.explanation: Los adjetivos cortos (una sílaba) forman el comparativo con -er + than: wide → wider. «More wide» no es correcto y «widest» es el superlativo.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «Mount Teide is ___ mountain in Spain.»
questions.explanation: El superlativo de los adjetivos cortos se forma con the + adjetivo + -est: the highest. Se usa al comparar un elemento con todos los de un grupo (in Spain).

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «Be quiet, please. The officer ___ to the witness right now.»
questions.explanation: «Right now» indica una acción que está ocurriendo en este momento, por lo que se usa el presente continuo: am/is/are + -ing (is talking).

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «My sister ___ speak three languages: Spanish, English and French.»
questions.explanation: Can expresa capacidad. Es un verbo modal: no añade -s en tercera persona, no lleva to y va seguido de infinitivo sin to (can speak).

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «The keys are ___ the table, next to the phone.»
questions.explanation: On indica que algo está sobre una superficie (on the table). In se usa para el interior de un espacio (in the drawer) y at para un punto concreto (at the door).

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «Maria is waiting outside. Can you tell ___ to come in?»
questions.explanation: Tras un verbo (tell) se usa el pronombre objeto: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. She es pronombre sujeto y hers es pronombre posesivo.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «Are there ___ questions before we start the exam?»
questions.explanation: En preguntas y frases negativas se usa normalmente any (Are there any questions?). Some se usa en afirmativas y en ofrecimientos; a solo va con singular contable.

questions.stem: Choose the best option: «You look very tired. You ___ go to bed earlier.»
questions.explanation: Should + infinitivo sin to sirve para dar consejos. Mustn't expresa prohibición y ningún modal va seguido de to (shouldn't to, would to son incorrectos).

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «We have already bought the tickets. We ___ visit London next summer.»
questions.explanation: Be going to + infinitivo expresa planes o intenciones ya decididos (ya tenemos los billetes). Falta el verbo be en «going to» y «will to» no existe.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «I ___ along the street when I saw the accident.»
questions.explanation: El pasado continuo (was/were + -ing) describe una acción en curso en el pasado que se ve interrumpida por otra en pasado simple (when I saw). Con I se usa was.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «If I ___ a lot of money, I would buy a house by the sea.»
questions.explanation: El segundo condicional expresa situaciones hipotéticas o poco probables en el presente: if + pasado simple, would + infinitivo (If I had…, I would buy…).

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «He can't drive yet. He isn't ___ to get a driving licence.»
questions.explanation: Enough va detrás del adjetivo (old enough) e indica que se alcanza el grado necesario. Too delante del adjetivo indica exceso (too old), lo que no tiene sentido aquí.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «She decided ___ a Guardia Civil officer after finishing school.»
questions.explanation: Algunos verbos como decide, want, hope, plan o promise van seguidos de infinitivo con to (decided to become). Otros, como enjoy o finish, llevan -ing.

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «The thief ___ by two officers last night.»
questions.explanation: La pasiva en pasado se forma con was/were + participio (was arrested). «Last night» exige pasado; «was arrest» no lleva participio.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence with the correct word order.
questions.explanation: Los adverbios de frecuencia (always, usually, never…) van detrás del verbo to be (She is always…) y delante de los demás verbos (She always arrives…).

questions.stem: What does «actually» mean in the sentence «I thought he was French, but actually he is Belgian»?
questions.explanation: Actually es un falso amigo: significa «en realidad» o «de hecho», no «actualmente» (que en inglés es currently, nowadays o at present).

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «___ it was raining, they went for a walk.»
questions.explanation: Although introduce una idea que contrasta con la principal (aunque llovía, salieron). However también expresa contraste, pero une dos oraciones independientes (It was raining. However, they went…), no una subordinada.

questions.stem: What does «give up» mean in the sentence «He gave up smoking two years ago»?
questions.explanation: El phrasal verb give up significa dejar de hacer algo o abandonar un hábito. No tiene relación con dar algo a otra persona (give).

questions.stem: Choose the correct question tag: «You have finished the report, ___?»
questions.explanation: El question tag repite el auxiliar de la oración en forma contraria: si la frase es afirmativa con have (have finished), la coletilla es negativa: haven't you?

questions.stem: Choose the correct option: «The road was closed, so we ___ take a different route.»
questions.explanation: Must no tiene forma de pasado; para expresar una obligación pasada se usa had to + infinitivo. «Musted» no existe.

questions.stem: Read the notice: «MUNICIPAL SWIMMING POOL – RULES. The pool is open every day from 10:00 to 20:00 from June to September. Children under 12 must be with an adult at all times. Please take a shower before you enter the water. Food and glass bottles are not allowed in the pool area. Lifeguards are on duty during opening hours; always follow their instructions.» When is the pool open?
options: Every day from 10:00 to 20:00, from June to September.
From Monday to Friday, from June to September.
questions.explanation: «The pool is open every day from 10:00 to 20:00 from June to September»: abre todos los días de 10:00 a 20:00 de junio a septiembre.

questions.stem: Read the notice: «MUNICIPAL SWIMMING POOL – RULES. The pool is open every day from 10:00 to 20:00 from June to September. Children under 12 must be with an adult at all times. Please take a shower before you enter the water. Food and glass bottles are not allowed in the pool area. Lifeguards are on duty during opening hours; always follow their instructions.» What must you do before you enter the water?
options: Show your ticket to a lifeguard.
Leave your bottles with an adult.
questions.explanation: «Please take a shower before you enter the water»: hay que ducharse antes de entrar en el agua.

questions.stem: Read the notice: «MUNICIPAL SWIMMING POOL – RULES. The pool is open every day from 10:00 to 20:00 from June to September. Children under 12 must be with an adult at all times. Please take a shower before you enter the water. Food and glass bottles are not allowed in the pool area. Lifeguards are on duty during opening hours; always follow their instructions.» Which of these can you NOT take into the pool area?
options: Your 10-year-old son, if you stay with him.
questions.explanation: «Food and glass bottles are not allowed»: no se permiten comida ni botellas de cristal. Un niño de 10 años puede entrar si está con un adulto.

questions.stem: Read the notice: «MUNICIPAL SWIMMING POOL – RULES. The pool is open every day from 10:00 to 20:00 from June to September. Children under 12 must be with an adult at all times. Please take a shower before you enter the water. Food and glass bottles are not allowed in the pool area. Lifeguards are on duty during opening hours; always follow their instructions.» What does «lifeguards are on duty» mean?
options: Swimmers must pay a fee to the lifeguards.
The lifeguards only work in the evening.
The people who watch the swimmers and help them are working.
questions.explanation: Lifeguard es el socorrista y «on duty» significa «de servicio»: los socorristas están trabajando durante todo el horario de apertura.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Elena is a nurse, but at weekends she volunteers with a mountain rescue team. Last Sunday the team received a call at six in the morning: two hikers were lost in the fog. Elena and four colleagues walked for three hours before they found them near a river. One of the hikers had hurt his ankle, so Elena gave him first aid. Then a helicopter took both hikers to the hospital. "It was a long day, but it is the best feeling in the world," Elena said.» What is Elena's job?
questions.explanation: «Elena is a nurse, but at weekends she volunteers with a mountain rescue team»: es enfermera y los fines de semana es voluntaria de rescate.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Elena is a nurse, but at weekends she volunteers with a mountain rescue team. Last Sunday the team received a call at six in the morning: two hikers were lost in the fog. Elena and four colleagues walked for three hours before they found them near a river. One of the hikers had hurt his ankle, so Elena gave him first aid. Then a helicopter took both hikers to the hospital. "It was a long day, but it is the best feeling in the world," Elena said.» How many people were in the rescue group that walked to find the hikers?
questions.explanation: «Elena and four colleagues walked for three hours»: Elena más cuatro compañeros son cinco personas.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Elena is a nurse, but at weekends she volunteers with a mountain rescue team. Last Sunday the team received a call at six in the morning: two hikers were lost in the fog. Elena and four colleagues walked for three hours before they found them near a river. One of the hikers had hurt his ankle, so Elena gave him first aid. Then a helicopter took both hikers to the hospital. "It was a long day, but it is the best feeling in the world," Elena said.» Why did Elena give first aid to one of the hikers?
options: Because he had fallen into the river.
Because he had hurt his ankle.
Because he was very cold after the night in the fog.
Because the helicopter could not arrive.
questions.explanation: «One of the hikers had hurt his ankle, so Elena gave him first aid»: so introduce la consecuencia; le atendió porque se había lesionado el tobillo.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Elena is a nurse, but at weekends she volunteers with a mountain rescue team. Last Sunday the team received a call at six in the morning: two hikers were lost in the fog. Elena and four colleagues walked for three hours before they found them near a river. One of the hikers had hurt his ankle, so Elena gave him first aid. Then a helicopter took both hikers to the hospital. "It was a long day, but it is the best feeling in the world," Elena said.» What does Elena think about the rescue?
options: It was tiring, but she feels very happy about it.
It was a waste of time.
questions.explanation: «It was a long day, but it is the best feeling in the world»: reconoce que fue un día largo (cansado), pero la experiencia le produce una gran satisfacción.

questions.stem: Read the radio report: «Good morning, here is the traffic information. There is heavy snow in the north, so drivers must use chains on the A-6 between kilometres 90 and 110. The N-232 is closed because of a lorry accident; police officers are directing traffic to a diversion through the village of Fuentes. In the south, the roads are clear but there may be fog early in the morning. Please drive carefully and check the information before you travel.» Why is the N-232 closed?
options: Because there has been a lorry accident.
questions.explanation: «The N-232 is closed because of a lorry accident»: está cortada por un accidente de camión (lorry = camión).

questions.stem: Read the radio report: «Good morning, here is the traffic information. There is heavy snow in the north, so drivers must use chains on the A-6 between kilometres 90 and 110. The N-232 is closed because of a lorry accident; police officers are directing traffic to a diversion through the village of Fuentes. In the south, the roads are clear but there may be fog early in the morning. Please drive carefully and check the information before you travel.» What must drivers do on the A-6 between kilometres 90 and 110?
options: Stop and wait for the police.
Drive with their fog lights only in the morning.
questions.explanation: «Drivers must use chains on the A-6 between kilometres 90 and 110»: must indica obligación; hay que poner cadenas por la nieve.

questions.stem: Read the radio report: «Good morning, here is the traffic information. There is heavy snow in the north, so drivers must use chains on the A-6 between kilometres 90 and 110. The N-232 is closed because of a lorry accident; police officers are directing traffic to a diversion through the village of Fuentes. In the south, the roads are clear but there may be fog early in the morning. Please drive carefully and check the information before you travel.» What is a «diversion» in this text?
options: A place where drivers can rest.
A different route that drivers must follow because a road is closed.
questions.explanation: Diversion es el desvío: una ruta alternativa por la que la policía dirige el tráfico porque la N-232 está cortada.

questions.stem: Read the radio report: «Good morning, here is the traffic information. There is heavy snow in the north, so drivers must use chains on the A-6 between kilometres 90 and 110. In the south, the roads are clear but there may be fog early in the morning. Please drive carefully and check the information before you travel.» Which statement about the south is true?
options: The roads are open, but it is possible that there will be fog early in the morning.
The roads are closed because of fog.
It is snowing heavily in the south.
Drivers must use chains in the south.
questions.explanation: «In the south, the roads are clear but there may be fog early in the morning»: clear significa despejadas y may expresa posibilidad (puede haber niebla).

questions.stem: Read the text: «On Tuesday afternoon, Mr Jones phoned the local police station because his dog, Max, had disappeared from the garden. He described Max as a small brown dog with a red collar. Two hours later, a woman found a dog with a red collar sleeping outside the supermarket. She called the number on the collar, and Mr Jones came to collect him. "I will never leave the garden gate open again," he promised.» How did Max probably leave the garden?
options: Someone stole him from the house.
He jumped out of a window.
Through the garden gate, which was open.
The woman took him to the supermarket.
questions.explanation: «I will never leave the garden gate open again»: Mr Jones promete no volver a dejar abierta la puerta del jardín, lo que indica que Max se escapó por ella.

questions.stem: Read the text: «Our school started a recycling project in October. Every classroom now has three bins: blue for paper, yellow for plastic and green for glass. Students in Year 3 check the bins every Friday and write the results on a chart. Since October, the school has reduced its rubbish by 40 per cent. Next term we are planning to grow vegetables in the school garden using compost from the canteen.» Which bin should you use for an empty plastic bottle?
questions.explanation: «Yellow for plastic»: el contenedor amarillo es para el plástico. El azul es para papel y el verde para vidrio.

Next term we are planning to grow vegetables in the school garden using compost from the canteen.» Which statement is true?
options: The school already grows vegetables in the garden.
The school produces less rubbish now than before October.
The school has reduced its rubbish to 40 per cent.
The recycling project will start next term.
questions.explanation: «Has reduced its rubbish by 40 per cent» significa que ha reducido la basura en un 40 % (ahora produce menos). El huerto es un plan para el próximo trimestre (are planning to) y el proyecto empezó en octubre.
